source_snapshot.scope: Associated compiler-input snapshot; hash association is not source-operand provenance.

entry_abi: candidate pointer in EAX; actual x86 call/return stack and callee-saved registers
input_policy: PE loaded at preferred base; only synthetic data/stack/RDRAM/table/name inputs and resolved lstrcatA IAT binding are changed; code bytes retained.
guards: Original hash and complete unforced candidate-manifest hash checked.
Unique MAP symbols and original-compatible frame/entry ABI required.
Every executed basic block must lie in the three reviewed bodies or begin at a modeled boundary.
Every emulated write must lie in the private stack, replacement table or count.
Full4096-byte replacement state checked against explicit expected values; RDRAM and code bytes unchanged.
Return stack and all callee-saved registers checked; instruction limit and unmapped-memory guards active.
boundary_model_scope: records are formatted fprintf attempts captured by the model, including when a negative return is injected; no real FILE buffering, filesystem persistence or GUI behavior is claimed. Volatile registers are deliberately clobbered at each modeled call.

original_history_slot.dataflow: Read value is tested for zero; it selects whether the same private slot retains start or is overwritten with the advanced hash cursor. No use reaches records, status, count, replacement table, or scan cursor.

limitations: Finite controlled inputs are not a universal equivalence proof.
CRT file/format functions, SetStatusText and lstrcatA are boundary models; real OS, CRT FILE internals, GUI and filesystem behavior are not exercised.
Only the stated normal bounded strings and synthetic tables are tested; undefined buffer-overflow inputs are excluded.
Preferred-base execution does not establish rebasing or source-operand provenance.
Behavioral agreement does not certify exact compiled bytes or recover original source declarations.
